newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Bank Corp posts loss, plans capital repayment.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Bank Corp posts loss, plans capital repayment.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp (SBC), as expected, reported a 1996 net loss as the result of a 3.3 billion Swiss franc ($2.2 billion) one-time charge, a change its method of accounting for credit provisions and a re-valuation of its real estate portfolio.
SBC, the country's third largest bank group, posted a group net loss of 1.955 billion francs ($1.3 billion) as compared to a 1.053 billion franc ($713.2 million) 1995 profit.

But it said gross operating profit was up 29 percent to 3.905 billion francs, net after-tax profit before extraordinary items was up 26 percent to 1.328 billion and it was confident of making further progress in 1997 toward its medium-term target of an after-tax Return On Equity (ROE) of 15 percent.
The group's 1996 after-tax ROE was 10.1 percent.

Separately, SBC said its board would propose to the annual general meeting that instead of a dividend for the 1996 financial year, it would make a capital repayment of 10 francs in nominal capital per registered share.
In addition, SBC said the biggest contribution to group profits came from SBC Private Banking, which increased net profit by nearly 19 percent to 1.063 billion francs.
The investment banking division SBC Warburg reported net profit growth of 55 percent to 820 million francs and generated an ROE of more than 16 percent.
Net interest income rose seven percent to 2.951 billion, fee and commission income increased by 31 percent to 4.374 billion and trading income was up 30 percent to 3.046 billion, SBC said.

"Against a background of low interst rates and attractive financial markets, Swiss Bank Corp is optimistic about the future progress of its businesses," SBC said in a statement. ($ = 1.476 Swiss Francs)
